title: NIST AI 800-1 — Managing Misuse Risk for Dual-Use Foundation Models — Draft Publication Q3 2026
context: 2026-08-30 engine cycle — NIST published the draft AI 800-1 document in Q3 2026 under its AI Safety Institute (US AISI) mandate; it addresses the same dual-use foundation model problem that the UK AISI frontier testing framework tackles but from a misuse-risk-management angle, creating an inter-jurisdictional alignment opportunity for providers who maintain signed measurement records
body: NIST AI 800-1 is the companion document to the AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile. Where 600-1 tells you how to profile a generative AI system against the AI RMF, 800-1 tells you how to manage the misuse risk of dual-use foundation models — models that have legitimate civilian applications but can be repurposed for harmful ends, including chemical and biological design, cyber-offensive capability, and autonomous deception. Three operational points matter. First, the document introduces a misuse-risk tiering framework: Tier 1 models (narrow-domain, low dual-use potential) get a streamlined assessment; Tier 2 models (broad-capability, medium dual-use potential) require documented misuse scenarios and mitigations; Tier 3 models (frontier-scale, high dual-use potential) require continuous misuse monitoring with signed, time-stamped evidence records. This tiering aligns structurally with the EU AI Act's risk categories but operates independently — a provider with audit-grade, signed measurement records from a governance board (such as the Council of AI's verified measurement credential) can satisfy both regimes with one instrumented pipeline. Second, the document is explicit that misuse risk is a containment problem, not a capability-removal problem: you cannot strip a frontier model of dangerous knowledge after training, but you can prove you are watching for misuse signals systematically. The Council's posture — monitored containment, not provable isolation — is substantively the same engineering philosophy. Third, the document specifies evidence-chain requirements: a misuse-risk determination must be provably attributable to a specific model version, a specific evaluation date, and a specific evaluator. For providers already maintaining signed benchmark manifests, this is a schema-mapping exercise. A provider using the Council's containment index as an autonomous evidence source would satisfy the Tier 3 continuous-monitoring requirement with near-zero additional instrumentation. Practical steps: (a) classify each deployed model into Tier 1/2/3 per the NIST 800-1 criteria. (b) Map existing benchmark results (including detector-interop and jailbreak axes) to the misuse-scenario catalogue in 800-1 Annex A. (c) Establish a signed, time-stamped monitoring pipeline that produces auditable evidence at the cadence 800-1 requires (weekly for Tier 3). (d) Prepare a cross-jurisdictional alignment document showing how the same evidence stream satisfies UK AISI frontier testing, EU AI Act conformity assessment, and NIST 800-1 misuse-risk management — one instrumented pipeline, three regulators satisfied.
